clue.text: Church's fury about non-ecclesiastical book

indicators.note: the church and fury pieces wrap around the word for non-clerical, so about signals going round

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
lay means not belonging to the clergy
fury is extreme anger

explanation.surface: A church's angry reaction to a secular book it disapproves of.
explanation.walkthrough: Clayhanger is Arnold Bennett's 1910 novel; 'non-ecclesiastical' is the lay, not clerical, sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold Bennett's novel of that title is a book, the first of his Potteries trilogy.

clue.text: One not totally quiet person in family car

indicators.note: the shortened timid person and the one sit inside the family word, so in signals containment

parts.note: a line is a family lineage
one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: not totally means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a mouse is a timid, quiet person

explanation.surface: Someone shy sitting in the family's car.
explanation.walkthrough: A quiet, timid person is called a mouse; 'not totally' trims its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is a large luxurious car, often chauffeur-driven.

clue.text: Long time taken to get to the point

parts.note: a year is a period of time
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: It took a long time to get round to the main point.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn for it: a verb synonym.

clue.text: Worshipping aloud ain't misbehaving

indicators.note: letters that misbehave do not stay in their proper order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone at a service praying loudly is behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' rearranges the letters of ALOUD and AINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulation is excessive admiration, a kind of worshipping of its object.

clue.text: Special show held for extremely honourable man

parts.note: a gala is a special festive show or occasion
had is the past tense of have, meaning held

explanation.surface: A special performance was put on for a highly honourable gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad, the purest knight of Arthurian legend, is a byword for a perfectly noble man.

clue.text: After uprising soldiers save capital

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising reads the pieces upwards, so the whole run is turned backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, part-time soldiers
save and bar both mean except

explanation.surface: Following a revolt, the troops rescue the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns TABAR upwards to read RABAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the capital city of Morocco.

clue.text: Action taken, for example

definitions.meaning: an action at law is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A deed was carried out, to give one instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A case is both a legal action and an instance or example of something.

clue.text: Kept woman from disparaging upper-class ancestor

indicators.note: read as dis-paraging, taking apart, it signals that the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A mistress whose low reputation comes from a snobbish forebear's sneers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disparaging' rearranges U and ANCESTOR; the word normally means belittling, here read as taking apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesan is a mistress kept by wealthy lovers, so a kept woman.

clue.text: Collection of papers diplomat kept in strongbox finally released

indicators.note: the diplomat is held inside the box, so kept in signals one piece placed within another
the last letter of the box word is let go, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a safe is a strongbox
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: Documents locked away by an ambassador are at last set free.
explanation.walkthrough: HE, His Excellency, is the courtesy title of an ambassador, hence a diplomat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheaf is a bundle of papers held together.

clue.text: Originally male university with men's college

indicators.note: read as in an original way, it says the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: men, with the possessive ending ignored

explanation.surface: A university college that was first for men only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' looks like 'at first' but here rearranges MALE, U and MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmanuel is a college of Cambridge University, founded in 1584.

clue.text: Kingdom's name finally changed to a sultanate?

indicators.note: the final letter of the engineer's surname is replaced by another

parts.note: Isambard Kingdom Brunel, the Victorian engineer, had the surname Brunel

explanation.surface: A kingdom renames itself a sultanate at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Kingdom is not a realm but the middle name of Isambard Kingdom Brunel; 'finally changed' swaps his last L for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei, on Borneo, is ruled by a sultan; the question mark marks it as one example of a sultanate.

clue.text: Before retiring woman expected to become a chaperon

indicators.note: the word for expected is placed before the reversed woman

parts.note: something due is expected

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman expected, before going to bed, to take on chaperoning duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like shy, but here it means going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman acting as chaperon to young girls, especially in Spain.

clue.text: Most attractive person in the latest gear

parts.note: hot means very new, the latest
stuff and gear both mean belongings or equipment

explanation.surface: The most attractive figure is wearing the newest fashions.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot stuff is informal for someone very sexy or attractive.

clue.text: Return match ending in brief quarrel

indicators.note: return means the word goes back, read in reverse

parts.note: to match is to fit

indicators.note: ending in picks the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A return game finishes in a short squabble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' reverses FIT to TIF; 'ending in' takes F from brief.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a minor, petty quarrel.

clue.text: Comprehensive school building used a good deal?

parts.note: full means complete, comprehensive
a house is a school boarding building

explanation.surface: A comprehensive school's building is heavily used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive school' suggests a British state school, but the words split; the definition is a card hand dealt in poker.
explanation.definitionFit: A full house is a strong poker hand, so a good deal of the cards.

clue.text: Brave as lion is in spell of bad fortune?

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior, once called an Indian
the lion, Leo, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A lion is courageous even during a run of bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian sign is a jinx or curse, an old American term for a spell of ill luck.

clue.text: One may be taken in shortly before tax year starts

definitions.text: One may be taken in shortly before tax year starts

parts.words: One may be taken in shortly before tax year starts
parts.note: a victim of a hoax on the first of the month, days before the British tax year begins on 6 April

explanation.walkthrough: The UK tax year starts on 6 April, so 1 April comes shortly before it; 'taken in' means fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tricked on the first of April is a dupe of that day's pranks.

clue.text: Source of report on old golfer that's explosive

parts.note: a gun produces a report, a loud bang
Henry Cotton was a British golfer, three-time Open champion between the 1930s and 1940s

explanation.surface: A gunshot heard near a veteran golfer suggests something explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Cotton was a famous British golfer of the mid-twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Guncotton is nitrocellulose, a highly explosive material.

clue.text: Very popular at all times? That's hard to believe!

parts.note: well in means in favour, very popular
ever means always

explanation.surface: Someone always popular provokes an exclamation of disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses astonishment at something surprising.

clue.text: Struggle fellow put up to defend head of that country

indicators.note: the pieces surround the letter, guarding it, so defend signals going round

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a man is a fellow

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter

explanation.surface: Fighting to protect the country's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defend' signals surrounding: the struggle and the upturned fellow guard the head of 'that' between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Vietnam is a country in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: It's doubly acceptable to reject what's far from acceptable

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the doubled word is reversed
doubly means the word appears twice

parts.note: on means acceptable, as in that's not on

explanation.surface: Something approved twice over still gets turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' gives ONON and 'to reject' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-no is something forbidden or unacceptable.

clue.text: Action he could be just beginning

indicators.note: could be says these letters might become something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: A man of action could just be getting started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges ACTION and HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchoate means only just begun, not yet fully formed.

clue.text: One stopping police informer's racket

indicators.note: the one stops up the word, plugging its middle

parts.note: a nose is slang for a police informer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone putting an end to a grass's criminal scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like a criminal scam; it means din. A nose is slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud noise, a din.

clue.text: Bizarre at one time? Not for a number of Romans

parts.note: anti means against, not for
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Was it strange in the past? Not to many Romans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at one time' flags an archaic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Antic once meant grotesque or bizarre, an old adjectival sense.

clue.text: Watch' cricket side's first appearance

parts.note: a look is an appearance
on is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: Watching a cricket team make its first appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is the half of the field behind the batter's legs. 'first' can only be a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: To look on is to watch as a spectator.

clue.text: Old British characters act badly after the game's up

indicators.note: the overacting word follows the reversed game
in a down clue up means read upwards, reversed

parts.note: Go is a board game
to ham is to overact

explanation.surface: Ancient Britons perform poorly once the match is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Go is the Japanese board game; 'up' fits a down clue, where reversal reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogham is an early medieval alphabet used for Old Irish and British inscriptions.

clue.text: Stimulate interest, at last, in card game

parts.note: to pique is to arouse or stimulate

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the preceding word

explanation.surface: Arousing curiosity at last in a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes T from interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Piquet is a two-handed card game.

clue.text: New convert, unorthodox type one church finally admitted

indicators.note: the church letter is let in, placed inside the rearranged letters
unorthodox means not in the usual order, so the letters are rearranged
finally picks the last letter

explanation.surface: A newly converted person of unconventional kind is finally let into church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' rearranges TYPEONE to NEOPYTE; 'admitted' takes in H, from 'finally' on church.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a novice, originally a new convert to a religion.

clue.text: Just monarch lying in state

indicators.note: the monarch lies in the state, placed inside it

parts.note: ME is the abbreviation for Maine, a US state
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: A fair king lies in state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying in state' suggests a royal funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means only or just, as in a mere child.

clue.text: In speech, express admiration for all who work on board

indicators.note: in speech means spoken, so a word that sounds the same is entered

parts.note: to compliment someone is to express admiration for them

explanation.surface: Praising everyone working aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone swaps an I for an E.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's complement is the full number of crew on board.
